In the thousand-sun network of humanity's expansion, new colony worlds are struggling to find their way. Every new planet lives on a knife edge between collapse and wonder, and the crew of the aging gunship Rocinante have their hands more than full keeping the fragile peace.

In the vast space between Earth and Jupiter, the inner planets and belt have formed a tentative and uncertain alliance still haunted by a history of wars and prejudices. On the lost colony world of Laconia, a hidden enemy has a new vision for all of humanity and the power to enforce it.

New technologies clash with old as the history of human conflict returns to its ancient patterns of war and subjugation. But human nature is not the only enemy, and the forces being unleashed have their own price. A price that will change the shape of humanity -- and of the Rocinante -- unexpectedly and forever. . .

books.title: The Left Hand of Darkness
books.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
books.desc:
[Comment by Kim Stanley Robinson, on The Guardian's website](https://www.theguardian.com/books/2011/may/14/science-fiction-authors-choice):
The Left Hand of Darkness by Ursula K Le Guin (1969)

> One of my favorite novels is The Left Hand of Darkness, by Ursula K Le Guin. For more than 40 years I've been recommending this book to people who want to try science fiction for the first time, and it still serves very well for that. One of the things I like about it is how clearly it demonstrates that science fiction can have not only the usual virtues and pleasures of the novel, but also the startling and transformative power of the thought experiment.

> In this case, the thought experiment is quickly revealed: "The king was pregnant," the book tells us early on, and after that we learn more and more about this planet named Winter, stuck in an ice age, where the humans are most of the time neither male nor female, but with the potential to become either. The man from Earth investigating this situation has a lot to learn, and so do we; and we learn it in the course of a thrilling adventure story, including a great "crossing of the ice". Le Guin's language is clear and clean, and has within it both the anthropological mindset of her father Alfred Kroeber, and the poetry of stories as magical things that her mother Theodora Kroeber found in native American tales. This worldly wisdom applied to the romance of other planets, and to human nature at its deepest, is Le Guin's particular gift to us, and something science fiction will always be proud of. Try it and see – you will never think about people in quite the same way again.

books.title: Pyramids
books.author: Terry Pratchett
books.desc: It's bad enough being new on the job, but Teppic hasn't a clue as to what a pharaoh is supposed to do. After all, he's been trained at Ankh-Morpork's famed assassins' school, across the sea from the Kingdom of the Sun.First, there's the monumental task of building a suitable resting place for Dad -- a pyramid to end all pyramids. Then there are the myriad administrative duties, such as dealing with mad priests, sacred crocodiles, and marching mummies. And to top it all off, the adolescent pharaoh discovers deceit, betrayal -- not to mention aheadstrong handmaiden -- at the heart of his realm.

books.title: Persepolis 1-4
books.author: Marjane Satrapi
books.desc: From inside front cover: The story of Satrapi's unforgettable childhood and coming of age within a ... loving family in Tehran during the Islamic Revolution; of the contradictions between private and public life in a coutnry plagued by political upheaval; of her high school years in Vienna facing the trails of adolescence far from her family; of her homecoming -- both sweet and terrible; and, finally, of her self-imposed exile from her beloved homeland.

books.title: Bad Blood
books.author: John Carreyrou
books.desc: Bad Blood: Secrets and Lies in a Silicon Valley Startup is a nonfiction book by journalist John Carreyrou, released May 21, 2018. It covers the rise and fall of Theranos, the multibillion-dollar biotech startup headed by Elizabeth Holmes. The book received critical acclaim, winning the 2018 Financial Times and McKinsey Business Book of the Year Award.

books.title: Permanent Record
books.author: Edward Snowden
books.desc:
Edward Snowden, the man who risked everything to expose the US government’s system of mass surveillance, reveals for the first time the story of his life, including how he helped to build that system and what motivated him to try to bring it down.

In 2013, twenty-nine-year-old Edward Snowden shocked the world when he broke with the American intelligence establishment and revealed that the United States government was secretly pursuing the means to collect every single phone call, text message, and email. The result would be an unprecedented system of mass surveillance with the ability to pry into the private lives of every person on earth. Six years later, Snowden reveals for the very first time how he helped to build this system and why he was moved to expose it.

Spanning the bucolic Beltway suburbs of his childhood and the clandestine CIA and NSA postings of his adulthood, Permanent Record is the extraordinary account of a bright young man who grew up online – a man who became a spy, a whistleblower, and, in exile, the Internet’s conscience. Written with wit, grace, passion, and an unflinching candor, Permanent Record is a crucial memoir of our digital age and destined to be a classic.

books.title: Don't Believe Everything You Think
books.author: Joseph Nguyen
books.desc:
Discover the book that has helped more than a million readers finally find relief from emotional suffering. Anxiety. Fear. Overthinking. Self-criticism. Is this painful mental state an unavoidable, hardwired fate for humans? Or can we find lasting peace, regardless of our circumstances? Don't Believe Everything You Think offers a radical yet simple idea: that the path to mental relief isn't through major behavioral change but through understanding how our mind creates our experience of life in the first place. Through an approach that is at once psychological, philosophical, and practical, Nguyen guides readers to a profound understanding of how destructive thinking patterns form -- and how to break them for good. The result? The ability to become emotionally resilient and free from anxiety at any moment. -- Back cover.

Learn how to overcome anxiety, self-doubt and self-sabotage without needing to rely on motivation or willpower. In this book, you'll discover the root cause of all psychological and emotional suffering and how to achieve freedom of mind to effortlessly create the life you've always wanted to live. Although pain is inevitable, suffering is optional. This book offers a completely new paradigm and understanding of where our human experience comes from, allowing us to end our own suffering and create how we want to feel at any moment. -- [josephnguyen.org](http://josephhguyen.org)

books.title: The Mountain Is You
books.author: Brianna Wiest
books.desc: This book is about self sabotage. Why we do it, when we do it, and how to stop doing it-for good. Coexisting but conflicting needs create self-sabotaging behaviors. This is why we resist efforts to change, often until they feel completely futile. But by extracting crucial insight from our most damaging habits, building emotional intelligence by better understanding our brains and bodies, releasing past experiences at a cellular level, and learning to act as our highest potential future selves, we can step out of our own way and into our potential. For centuries, the mountain has been used as a metaphor for the big challenges we face, especially ones that seem impossible to overcome. To scale our mountains, we actually have to do the deep internal work of excavating trauma, building resilience, and adjusting how we show up for the climb. In the end, it is not the mountain we master, but ourselves.

books.title: Getting Things Done
books.author: David Allen
books.desc: In today's world, yesterday's methods just don't work. In Getting Things Done, veteran coach and management consultant David Allen shares the breakthrough methods for stress-free performance that he has introduced to tens of thousands of people across the country. Allen's premise is simple: our productivity is directly proportional to our ability to relax. Only when our minds are clear and our thoughts are organized can we achieve effective productivity and unleash our creative potential.

books.title: Island of the Blue Dolphins
books.author: Scott O’Dell
books.desc:
Story of a young girl abandoned on a small island by her family and her village, and of her fight for survival.

The incredible courage, determination and strength of this girl is showcased throughout as she learns to do the things that only the men of her tribe did before, and battles not only the hunters who frequent the island, but also her desperate loneliness as well...

Excellent read for kids 11 and older.

books.title: The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat
books.author: Oliver Sacks
books.desc:
In his most extraordinary book, “one of the great clinical writers of the twentieth century” *(The New York Times)* recounts the case histories of patients lost in the bizarre, apparently inescapable world of neurological disorders. 

Oliver Sacks’s *The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat* tells the stories of individuals afflicted with fantastic perceptual and intellectual aberrations: patients who have lost their memories and with them the greater part of their pasts; who are no longer able to recognize people and common objects; who are stricken with violent tics and grimaces or who shout involuntary obscenities; whose limbs have become alien; who have been dismissed as retarded yet are gifted with uncanny artistic or mathematical talents. 

If inconceivably strange, these brilliant tales remain, in Dr. Sacks’s splendid and sympathetic telling, deeply human. They are studies of life struggling against incredible adversity, and they enable us to enter the world of the neurologically impaired, to imagine with our hearts what it must be to live and feel as they do. A great healer, Sacks never loses sight of medicine’s ultimate responsibility: “the suffering, afflicted, fighting human subject.”

books.title: La sombra del viento
books.author: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
books.desc:
Un amanecer de 1945, un muchacho es conducido por su padre a un misterioso lugar oculto en el corazón de la ciudad vieja: el Cementerio de los Libros Olvidados. Allí, Daniel Sempere encuentra un libro maldito que cambia el rumbo de su vida y le arrastra a un laberinto de intrigas y secretos enterrados en el alma oscura de la ciudad. La Sombra del Viento es un misterio literario ambientado en la Barcelona de la primera mitad del siglo xx, desde los últimos esplendores del Modernismo hasta las tinieblas de la posguerra.

Aunando las técnicas del relato de intriga y suspense, la novela histórica y la comedia de costumbres, La Sombra del Viento es sobre todo una trágica historia de amor cuyo eco se proyecta a través del tiempo. Con gran fuerza narrativa, el autor entrelaza tramas y enigmas a modo de muñecas rusas en un inolvidable relato sobre los secretos del corazón y el embrujo de los libros cuya intriga se mantiene hasta la última página.

Todavía recuerdo aquel amanecer en que mi padre me llevó por primera vez a visitar El Cementerio de los Libros Olvidados

books.title: Forbidden knowledge
books.author: Roger Shattuck
books.desc:
Forbidden Knowledge boldly traces the tragic arc of Western literature and culture as it explores the notion of "forbidden knowledge," from the sexual innocence of Adam and Eve to the awe-inspiring discoveries of modern scientists who have created the atomic bomb and recombinant DNA. The result is a dire portrait of human presumption and of a culture that has abandoned all limits in the quest for knowledge and experience.

The harrowing imagery that Shattuck presents is matched only by his faith that we can understand our grievous loss of innocence by reexamining our greatest myths and stories of the last two thousand years. In lively, lucid prose Shattuck explores our uncertain fate through such myths as that of Prometheus and a wide range of literary works, including Milton's Paradise Lost, the writings of the Marquis de Sade, Mary Shelley's Frankenstein, Melville's Billy Budd, and the poetry of Emily Dickinson.

Parents and teachers should be aware that Chapter VII does not make appropriate reading for children and minors.

In this seminal work, Shattuck breaks new ground in opening up a crucial subject never before accorded this full-scale treatment. Forbidden Knowledge impels us to a renewed effort to think judiciously about morality and the sacred during a decade of radical skepticism. Forbidden Knowledge represents the capstone of Roger Shattuck's career as one of America's most original and gifted thinkers.

books.title: The Silence of the Lambs
books.author: Thomas Harris
books.desc:
The Silence of the Lambs is a psychological horror novel by Thomas Harris. First published in 1988, it is the sequel to Harris's 1981 novel Red Dragon. Both novels feature the cannibalistic serial killer Dr. Hannibal Lecter, this time pitted against FBI Special Agent Clarice Starling. 

The novel won the 1988 Bram Stoker Award for Best Novel.
The novel also won the 1989 Anthony Award for Best Novel.
It was nominated for the 1989 World Fantasy Award.
----------
Also contained in:

 - [Red Dragon / The Silence of the Lambs](https://openlibrary.org/works/OL138391W)

books.title: Cinder
books.author: Marissa Meyer
books.desc:
Humans and androids crowd the raucous streets of New Beijing. A deadly plague ravages the population. From space, a ruthless lunar people watch, waiting to make their move. No one knows that Earth's fate hinges on one girl. . . .
Cinder, a gifted mechanic, is a cyborg. She's a second-class citizen with a mysterious past, reviled by her stepmother and blamed for her stepsister's illness. But when her life becomes intertwined with the handsome Prince Kai's, she suddenly finds herself at the center of an intergalactic struggle, and a forbidden attraction. Caught between duty and freedom, loyalty and betrayal, but mostly a forbidden love, she must uncover secrets about her past in order to protect her world's future.

books.title: Fun Home
books.author: Alison Bechdel
books.desc:
A fresh and brilliantly told memoir from a cult favorite comic artist, marked by gothic twists, a family funeral home, sexual angst, and great books.

This breakout book by Alison Bechdel is a darkly funny family tale, pitch-perfectly illustrated with Bechdel's sweetly gothic drawings. Like Marjane Satrapi's Persepolis, it's a story exhilaratingly suited to graphic memoir form.

Meet Alison's father, a historic preservation expert and obsessive restorer of the family's Victorian home, a third-generation funeral home director, a high school English teacher, an icily distant parent, and a closeted homosexual who, as it turns out, is involved with his male students and a family babysitter. Through narrative that is alternately heartbreaking and fiercely funny, we are drawn into a daughter's complex yearning for her father. And yet, apart from assigned stints dusting caskets at the family-owned "fun home," as Alison and her brothers call it, the relationship achieves its most intimate expression through the shared code of books. When Alison comes out as homosexual herself in late adolescense, the denouement is swift, graphic -- and redemptive.

books.title: Lock In: A Novel of the Near Future (Lock In Series Book 1)
books.author: John Scalzi
books.desc: "Fifteen years from now, a new virus sweeps the globe. 95% of those afflicted experience nothing worse than fever and headaches. Four percent suffer acute meningitis, creating the largest medical crisis in history. And one percent find themselves "locked in"--fully awake and aware, but unable to move or respond to stimulus. One per cent doesn't seem like a lot. But in the United States, that's 1.7 million people "locked in"...including the President's wife and daughter. Spurred by grief and the sheer magnitude of the suffering, America undertakes a massive scientific initiative. Nothing can restore the ability to control their own bodies to the locked in. But then two new technologies emerge. One is a virtual-reality environment, "The Agora," in which the locked-in can interact with other humans, both locked-in and not. The other is the discovery that a few rare individuals have brains that are receptive to being controlled by others, meaning that from time to time, those who are locked in can "ride" these people and use their bodies as if they were their own. This skill is quickly regulated, licensed, bonded, and controlled. Nothing can go wrong. Certainly nobody would be tempted to misuse it, for murder, for political power, or worse....John Scalzi's Lock In is a novel of our near future, from one of the most popular authors in modern science fiction"--

books.title: Heretics of Dune
books.author: Frank Herbert
books.desc: With more than ten million copies sold, Frank Herbert's magnificent Dune books stand among the major achievements of the human imagination. In this, the fifth and most spectacular Dune book of all, the planet Arrakis--now called Rakis--is becoming desert again. The Lost Ones are returning home from the far reaches of space. The great sandworms are dying. And the children of Dune's children awaken from empire as from a dream, wielding the new power of a heresy called love...

books.title: Simon vs. the Homo Sapiens Agenda
books.author: Becky Albertalli
books.desc:
Sixteen-year-old and not-so-openly gay Simon Spier prefers to save his drama for the school musical. But when an email falls into the wrong hands, his secret is at risk of being thrust into the spotlight. Now Simon is actually being blackmailed: if he doesn’t play wingman for class clown Martin, his sexual identity will become everyone’s business. Worse, the privacy of Blue, the pen name of the boy he’s been emailing, will be compromised.

With some messy dynamics emerging in his once tight-knit group of friends, and his email correspondence with Blue growing more flirtatious every day, Simon’s junior year has suddenly gotten all kinds of complicated. Now, change-averse Simon has to find a way to step out of his comfort zone before he’s pushed out—without alienating his friends, compromising himself, or fumbling a shot at happiness with the most confusing, adorable guy he’s never met.

books.title: Crónica de una muerte anunciada
books.author: Gabriel García Márquez
books.desc:
Also contained in:

- [Collected Novellas](https://openlibrary.org/works/OL274508W)

books.title: Kitchen Confidential
books.author: Anthony Bourdain
books.desc: A celebrity chef shares anecdotes of his experience in the restaurant industry, and of his journey from dishwasher to a position of fame in the food industry.

books.title: The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin
books.author: Benjamin Franklin
books.desc:
Few men could compare to Benjamin Franklin. Virtually self-taught, he excelled as an athlete, a man of letters, a printer, a scientist, a wit, an inventor, an editor, and a writer, and he was probably the most successful diplomat in American history. David Hume hailed him as the first great philosopher and great man of letters in the New World.

Written initially to guide his son, Franklin's autobiography is a lively, spellbinding account of his unique and eventful life. Stylistically his best work, it has become a classic in world literature, one to inspire and delight readers everywhere.

books.title: The Island of Dr. Moreau
books.author: H. G. Wells
books.desc:
Ranked among the classic novels of the English language and the inspiration for several unforgettable movies, this early work of H. G. Wells was greeted in 1896 by howls of protest from reviewers, who found it horrifying and blasphemous. They wanted to know more about the wondrous possibilities of science shown in his first book, The Time Machine, not its potential for misuse and terror. In The Island of Dr. Moreau, a shipwrecked gentleman named Edward Prendick, stranded on a Pacific island lorded over by the notorious Dr. Moreau, confronts dark secrets, strange creatures, and a reason to run for his life.

While this riveting tale was intended to be a commentary on evolution, divine creation, and the tension between human nature and culture, modern readers familiar with genetic engineering will marvel at Wells’s prediction of the ethical issues raised by producing “smarter” human beings or bringing back extinct species. These levels of interpretation add a richness to Prendick’s adventures on Dr. Moreau’s island of lost souls without distracting from what is still a rip-roaring good read.

books.title: Witches Abroad
books.author: Terry Pratchett
books.desc: Be careful what you wish for...Once upon a time there was a fairy godmother named Desiderata who had a good heart, a wise head, and poor planning skills—which unforunately left the Princess Emberella in the care of her other (not quite so good and wise) godmother when DEATH came for Desiderata. So now it's up to Magrat Garlick, Granny Weatherwax, and Nanny Ogg to hop on broomsticks and make for far-distant Genua to ensure the servant girl doesn't marry the Prince.But the road to Genua is bumpy, and along the way the trio of witches encounters the occasional vampire, werewolf, and falling house (well this is a fairy tale, after all). The trouble really begins once these reluctant foster-godmothers arrive in Genua and must outwit their power-hungry counterpart who'll stop at nothing to achieve a proper "happy ending"—even if it means destroying a kingdom.

books.title: How the Grinch Stole Christmas!
books.author: Dr. Seuss
books.desc: The Grinch tries to stop Christmas from arriving by stealing all the presents and food from the village, but much to his surprise it comes anyway. Could Christmas be more than presents?

books.title: Duma Key
books.author: Stephen King
books.desc: Duma Key is a novel by American writer Stephen King published on January 22, 2008 by Scribner. The book reached No. 1 on the New York Times Best Seller List. It is King's first novel to be set in Florida and/or Minnesota.

books.title: Uprooted
books.author: Naomi Novik
books.desc: "Our Dragon doesn't eat the girls he takes, no matter what stories they tell outside our valley. We hear them sometimes, from travelers passing through. They talk as though we were doing human sacrifice, and he were a real dragon. Of course that's not true: he may be a wizard and immortal, but he's still a man, and our fathers would band together and kill him if he wanted to eat one of use every ten years. He protects us against the Wood, and we're grateful, but not that grateful."

books.title: Kindred
books.author: Octavia E. Butler
books.desc: Dana, a modern black woman, is celebrating her twenty-sixth birthday with her new husband when she is snatched abruptly from her home in California and transported to the antebellum South. Rufus, the white son of a plantation owner, is drowning, and Dana has been summoned to save him. Dana is drawn back repeatedly through time to the slave quarters, and each time the stay grows longer, more arduous, and more dangerous until it is uncertain whether or not Dana’s life will end, long before it has a chance to begin.

books.title: The Glass Castle
books.author: Jeannette Walls
books.desc: A story about the early life of Jeannette Walls. The memoir is an exposing work about her early life and growing up on the run and often homeless. It presents a different perspective of life from all over the United States and the struggle a girl had to find normalcy as she grew into an adult.

books.title: I Have No Mouth and I Must Scream
books.author: Harlan Ellison
books.desc: This is a story set in a post-apocalyptic future. The Cold War progressed until it was too complicated for humans to manage, so the three major superpowers each developed a computer program to help run the war. When one of the programs becomes sentient it eliminates all of the human race except five persons, which it tortures for eternity.

books.title: Czas pogardy
books.author: Andrzej Sapkowski
books.desc: Świat Ciri i wiedźmina ogarniają płomienie. Nastał zapowiadany przez Ithlinne czas miecza i topora - czas pogardy. A w czasach pogardy na powierzchnię wypełzają Szczury, atakujące po szczurzemu, cicho, zdradziecko i okrutnie. To maruderzy z rozbitych armii, zabłąkane dzieciaki, zgwałcone dziewczyny, wieśniacy, których obejścia spalono, a rodziny wymordowano. Wyrzutki, dziwna zbieranina stworzona przez wojnę i na wojennym nieszczęściu żerująca.

books.title: Heidi
books.author: Spyri, Johanna
books.desc:
***The famous Swiss classic about Heidi, a five-year-old orphan girl*** who goes to live with her grandfather, and his goats, in an alm (Alpine pasture)...up the Alps. **One of the most loved classics ...both by children and adults, alike.**

***Little orphan Heidi goes to live high in the Alps with her gruff grandfather and brings happiness to all who know her on the mountain. When Heidi goes to Frankfurt to work in a wealthy household, she dreams of returning to the mountains and meadows, her friend Peter, and her beloved grandfather.***

books.title: Christine
books.author: Stephen King
books.desc:
A love triangle involving 17-year-old misfit Arnie Cunningham, his new girlfriend and a haunted 1958 Plymouth Fury. Dubbed Christine by her previous owner, Arnie's first car is jealous, possessive and deadly. 
([source][1])


  [1]: https://stephenking.com/library/novel/christine.html

books.title: Anthem
books.author: Ayn Rand
books.desc:
Anthem is a tale of a future dark age of the great “we” – a world that deprives individuals of name, independence, and values.

He lived in the dark ages of the future. In a loveless world he dared to love the woman of his choice. In an age that had lost all traces of science and civilization he had the courage to seek and find knowledge. But these were not the crimes for which he would be hunted He was marked for death because he had committed the unpardonable sin: He had stood forth from the mindless human herd. He was alone.

books.title: Анна Каренина
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.desc: Described by William Faulkner as the best novel ever written and by Fyodor Dostoevsky as “flawless,” Anna Karenina tells of the doomed love affair between the sensuous and rebellious Anna and the dashing officer, Count Vronsky. Tragedy unfolds as Anna rejects her passionless marriage and thereby exposes herself to the hypocrisies of society. Set against a vast and richly textured canvas of nineteenth-century Russia, the novel's seven major characters create a dynamic imbalance, playing out the contrasts of city and country life and all the variations on love and family happiness.

books.title: Мы
books.author: Евгений Иванович Замятин
books.desc:
Wikipedia

We is set in the future. D-503, a spacecraft engineer, lives in the One State, an urban nation constructed almost entirely of glass, which assists mass surveillance. The structure of the state is Panopticon-like, and life is scientifically managed F. W. Taylor-style. People march in step with each other and are uniformed. There is no way of referring to people except by their given numbers. The society is run strictly by logic or reason as the primary justification for the laws or the construct of the society. The individual's behavior is based on logic by way of formulas and equations outlined by the One State.

We is a dystopian novel completed in 1921. It was written in response to the author's personal experiences with the Russian revolutions of 1905 and 1917, his life in the Newcastle suburb of Jesmond and work in the Tyne shipyards at nearby Wallsend during the First World War. It was at Tyneside that he observed the rationalization of labor on a large scale.

books.title: Interesting Times
books.author: Terry Pratchett
books.desc: "May you live in interesting times" is the worst thing one can wish on a citizen of Discworld -- especially on the distinctly unmagical sorcerer Rincewind, who has had far too much perilous excitement in his life. But when a request for a "Great Wizzard" arrives in Ankh-Morpork via carrier albatross from the faraway Counterweight Continent, it's he who's sent as emissary. Chaos threatens to follow the impending demise of the Agatean Empire's current ruler. And, for some incomprehensible reason, someone believes Rincewind will have a mythic role in the war and wholesale bloodletting that will surely ensue. (Carnage is pretty much a given, since Cohen the Barbarian and his extremely elderly Silver Horde are busily formulating their own plan for looting, pillaging, and, er, looking wistfully at girls.) However, Rincewind firmly believes there are too many heroes already in the world, yet only one Rincewind. And he owes it to the world to keep that one alive for as long as possible.

books.title: The Lathe of Heaven
books.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
books.desc:
“The Lathe of Heaven” ; 1971 ( Ursula Le Guin received the 1973 Locus Award for this story)
George Orr has a gift – he is an effective dreamer:  his dreams become reality when he wakes up. He is aware of his past and present, two or more sets of memories, although the people around him are only aware of the current reality. 
This science fiction story is set in Portland, Oregon, in/around the late 1990s - early 2000s.  Orr begins to take drugs to suppress dreams but eventually he is sent to a psychotherapist, Dr. William Haber, who has developed an electronic  machine, the Augmentor, which records the brain patterns of a person as they dream.  When Haber realizes that he can use Orr's unique ability to change their world, the consequences  are both beneficial and frightening,  both locally and globally.  Orr seeks out the help of a civil rights lawyer, Heather Lelache, who attends a treatment session, and sees Portland change before her very eyes as Orr awakens.  In a strange turn of events, Heather helps Orr by putting him in a dream state where Orr can undo some of Haber's actions. The result – Aliens on the Moon land on Earth !  A special affinity exists between George Orr and the Aliens, who seem to understand  his unique gift.   Ultimately Haber decides to impose Orr's brain patterns on his own, so that he can bring about world-wide changes. Orr and Heather feel the chaos and a sense of a void as Haber dreams.  Orr rushes back to Haber's office and turns off the Augmentor.  The world  returns to April 1998.

books.title: Middlesex
books.author: Jeffrey Eugenides
books.desc: A unique coming of age story. While the main character in this novel is dealing with gender identity issues the main focus of this brilliantly written story is the confusion we all face as we grow into the person we were meant to be.  The reader finds himself identifying with the main character's experiences. This is a brilliantly written story. The prose is honest in a way that few authors dare to write. Every word, every action, every thought, is symbolic of the common human experience.

books.title: The Underground Railroad
books.author: Colson Whitehead
books.desc:
Cora is a slave on a cotton plantation in Georgia. Life is hell for all the slaves, but especially bad for Cora; an outcast even among her fellow Africans, she is coming into womanhood—where even greater pain awaits. When Caesar, a recent arrival from Virginia, tells her about the Underground Railroad, they decide to take a terrifying risk and escape. Matters do not go as planned—Cora kills a young white boy who tries to capture her. Though they manage to find a station and head north, they are being hunted.
     In Whitehead’s ingenious conception, the Underground Railroad is no mere metaphor—engineers and conductors operate a secret network of tracks and tunnels beneath the Southern soil. Cora and Caesar’s first stop is South Carolina, in a city that initially seems like a haven. But the city’s placid surface masks an insidious scheme designed for its black denizens. And even worse: Ridgeway, the relentless slave catcher, is close on their heels. Forced to flee again, Cora embarks on a harrowing flight, state by state, seeking true freedom.
     Like the protagonist of Gulliver’s Travels, Cora encounters different worlds at each stage of her journey—hers is an odyssey through time as well as space. As Whitehead brilliantly re-creates the unique terrors for black people in the pre–Civil War era, his narrative seamlessly weaves the saga of America from the brutal importation of Africans to the unfulfilled promises of the present day. The Underground Railroad is at once a kinetic adventure tale of one woman’s ferocious will to escape the horrors of bondage and a shattering, powerful meditation on the history we all share.

books.title: कामसूत्र
books.author: Vatsyāyana
books.desc: A work of philosophy, psychology, sociology, Hindu dogma, scientific inquiry, and sexology, the "Kama Sutra" has been a classic of world literature for more than 1700 years.

books.title: Start with why
books.author: Simon Sinek
books.desc: The most important question for any organization There's a naturally occurring pattern shared by the people and organizations that achieve the greatest long-term success. From Martin Luther King Jr. to Steve Jobs, from the pioneers of aviation to the founders of Southwest Airlines, the most inspiring leaders think, act, and communicate the exact same way—and it's the complete opposite of everyone else.The common thread, according to Simon Sinek, is that they all start with why. This simple question has the power to inspire others to achieve extraordinary things.Any organization can explain what it does; some can explain how; but very few can clearly articulate why. Why do we offer these particular products or services? Why do our customers choose us? Why do our employees stay (or leave)? Once you have those answers, teams get stronger, the mission clicks into place, and the path ahead becomes much clearer.Starting with why is the key to everything from putting a man on the moon to launching the iPod. Drawing on a wide range of fascinating examples, Sinek shows readers how to apply why to their culture, hiring decisions, product development, sales, marketing, and many other challenges. Some naturally think this way, but Sinek proves that anyone can learn how.

books.title: Rework
books.author: Jason Fried
books.desc: Most business books give you the same old advice: Write a business plan, study the competition, seek investors, yadda yadda. If you're looking for a book like that, put this one back on the shelf.Rework shows you a better, faster, easier way to succeed in business. Read it and you'll know why plans are actually harmful, why you don't need outside investors, and why you're better off ignoring the competition. The truth is, you need less than you think. You don't need to be a workaholic. You don't need to staff up. You don't need to waste time on paperwork or meetings. You don't even need an office. Those are all just excuses.  What you really need to do is stop talking and start working. This book shows you the way. You'll learn how to be more productive, how to get exposure without breaking the bank, and tons more counterintuitive ideas that will inspire and provoke you.With its straightforward language and easy-is-better approach, Rework is the perfect playbook for anyone who's ever dreamed of doing it on their own. Hardcore entrepreneurs, small-business owners, people stuck in day jobs they hate, victims of "downsizing," and artists who don't want to starve anymore will all find valuable guidance in these pages.From the Hardcover edition.

books.title: Mrs. Dalloway
books.author: Virginia Woolf
books.desc:
Virginia Woolf’s novel chronicles a day in the life of Clarissa Dalloway, a politician’s wife in 1920s London, as she prepares to host a party that evening. The narrative follows Clarissa’s thoughts (and sometimes those of people she meets) as she goes about her errands, and events in the day remind her of her youth and friendships from the past. As the book progresses characters from the past emerge, igniting old feelings and making Clarissa question the life she has created for herself.

*Mrs. Dalloway* became the inspiration for Michael Cunningham’s 1998 novel *The Hours*.

books.title: Beowulf
books.author: Seamus Heaney
books.desc: Composed toward the end of the first millennium, Beowulf is the elegiac narrative of the adventures of Beowulf, a Scandinavian hero who saves the Danes from the seemingly invincible monster Grendel and, later, from Grendel's mother. He then returns to his own country and dies in old age in a vivid fight against a dragon. The poem is about encountering the monstrous, defeating it, and then having to live on in the exhausted aftermath. In the contours of this story, at once remote and uncannily familiar at the beginning of the twenty-first century, Nobel laureate Seamus Heaney finds a resonance that summons power to the poetry from deep beneath its surface. Drawn to what he has called the "four-squareness of the utterance" in Beowulf and its immense emotional credibility, Heaney gives these epic qualities new and convincing reality for the contemporary reader.

books.title: Lonesome Dove
books.author: Larry McMurtry
books.desc:
Lonesome Dove, by Larry McMurtry, the author of Terms of Endearment, is his long-awaited masterpiece, the major noel at last of the American West as it really was.

A love story, an adventure, an American epic, Lonesome Dove embraces all the West--legend and fact, heroes and outlaws, whores and ladies, Indians and settlers--in a novel that recreates the Central American experience, the most enduring of our national myths.

Set in the late nineteenth century. Lonesome Dove is the story of a cattle drive from Texas to Montana -- and much more. It is a drive that represents for everybody involved not only a Darin, even a foolhardy, adventure, but a part of the American Dream--the attempt to carve out of the last remaining wilderness a new life.

Augustus McCrae and W. F. Call are former Texas Rangers, partners and friends who have shared hardship and danger together without ever quite understanding (or wanting to understand) each other's deepest emotions. Gus is the romantic, a reluctant rancher who has a way with women and the sense to leave well enough alone. Call is a driven, demanding man, a natural authority figure with no patience for weakness, and not many of his own. He is obsessed with the dream of creating his own empire, and with the need to conceal a secret sorrow of his own. The two men could hardly be more different, but both are tough, redoubtable fighters who have learned to count on each other, if nothing else. 

Call's dream not only drags Gus along in its wake, but draws in a vast cast of characters:
-Lorena, the whore with the proverbial heart of gold, whom Gus (and almost everyone else) loves, and who. Survives one of the most terrifying experiences any woman could have...
-Elmira, the restless, reluctant wife of a small-time Arkansas sheriff, who runs away from the security of marriage to become part of the great Western adventure...
--Blue Duck, the sinister Indian renegade, one of the most frightening villains in American fiction, whose steely capacity for cruelty affects the lives of everyone in the book...
-Newt, the young cowboy for whom the long and dangerous journey from Texas to Montana is in fact a search for his own identity...
-Jake, the dashing, womanising ex-ranger, a comrade-in-arms of Gus and Call, whose weakness leads him to an unexpected fate...
-July Johnson, husband of Elmira, whose love for her draws him out of his secure life into a kind of hero...

Lonesome Dove seeps from the Rio Grande (where Gus and Call acquire the cattle for their long drive by raiding the Mexicans) to the Montana highlands (where they find themselves besieged by the last, defiant remnants of an older West).

It is an epic of love, heroism, loyalty, honour, and betrayal--faultlessly written, unfailingly dramatic. Lonesome Dove is the novel about the West that American literature--and the American reader--has long been waiting for.
--jacket


----------
Contains:

 - [Lonesome Dove: 2/2](https://openlibrary.org/works/OL134565W)

books.title: The Vampire Lestat
books.author: Anne Rice
books.desc: The Vampire Lestat (1985) is a vampire novel by American writer Anne Rice, the second in her Vampire Chronicles, following Interview with the Vampire (1976). The story is told from the point of view of the vampire Lestat de Lioncourt as narrator, while Interview is narrated by Louis de Pointe du Lac. Several events in the two books appear to contradict each other, allowing the reader to decide which version of events they believe to be accurate.

books.title: A Darker Shade of Magic
books.author: V. E. Schwab
books.desc:
STEP INTO A UNIVERSE OF DARING ADVENTURE, THRILLING POWER, AND MULTIPLE LONDONS.

Kell is one of the last travelers--magicians with a rare, coveted ability to travel between parallel universes connected by one magic city.

There's Grey London, dirty and boring, without any magic, and with one mad king--George III. Red London, where life and magic are revered--and where Kell was raised alongside Rhy Maresh, the roguish heir to a flourishing empire. White London--a place where people fight to control magic and the magic fights back, draining the city to its very bones. And once upon a time, there was Black London. But no one speaks of that now.

Officially, Kell is the Red Traveler, ambassador of the Maresh Empire, carrying the monthly correspondences between the royals of each London. Unofficially, Kell is a smuggler, servicing people willing to pay for even the smallest glimpses of a world they'll never see. It's a defiant hobby with dangerous consequences, which Kell is now seeing firsthand.

Fleeing into Grey London, Kell runs into Delilah Bard, a cutpurse with lofty aspirations. She first robs him, then saves him from a deadly enemy, and finally forces Kell to spirit  her to another world for a proper adventure.

Now perilous magic is afoot, and treachery lurks at every turn. To save all of the worlds, they'll first need to stay alive.

This description comes from the publisher. *A Darker Shade of Magic* is the first book of the Shades of Magic trilogy.

books.title: Children of Dune
books.author: Frank Herbert
books.desc: The science fiction masterpiece continues in the "major event,"( Los Angeles Times) Children of Dune. With millions of copies sold worldwide, Frank Herbert's Dune novels stand among the major achievements of the human imagination and one of the most significant sagas in the history of literary science fiction. The Children of Dune are twin siblings Leto and Ghanima Atreides, whose father, the Emperor Paul Muad'Dib, disappeared in the deserts of Arrakis. Like their father, they possess supernormal abilities—making them valuable to their aunt Alia, who rules the Empire. If Alia can obtain the secrets of the twins' prophetic visions, her rule will be absolute. But the twins have their own plans for their destiny.

What's the only cure for the meanest grandmother in the world? George creates a fierce and fantastic bubbling brew, the perfect cure.

In this popular Dahl story, George creates a very special medicine to cure his grandma of her nasty habits. Great new Quentin Blake cover as well as a whole new exciting end section about Roald Dahl and his world.

books.title: The Big Sleep
books.author: Raymond Chandler
books.desc: Philip Marlowe, a private eye who operates in Los Angeles's seamy underside during the 1930s, takes on his first case, which involves a paralyzed California millionaire, two psychotic daughters, blackmail, and murder

books.title: Il pendolo di Foucault
books.author: Umberto Eco
books.desc:
*Il pendolo di Foucault* è il secondo romanzo dello scrittore italiano Umberto Eco. Pubblicato nel 1988 dalla casa editrice Bompiani (con cui Eco aveva già un pluridecennale rapporto), è ambientato negli anni della vita dello scrittore, fino ai primi anni ottanta. *Il pendolo di Foucault* è suddiviso in dieci segmenti che rappresentano le dieci Sephirot. Il romanzo è ricco di citazioni esoteriche, dalla Cabala all'alchimia e alla teoria del complotto, così tante che il critico letterario e romanziere Anthony Burgess ha suggerito che sarebbe stato utile un indice.


----------


Extraordinary narrative by Italian semiotician and professor Umberto Eco, who guides us through the darkest corners of history.

books.title: A Discovery of Witches
books.author: Deborah Harkness
books.desc:
**An epic, richly inventive, historically sweeping, magical romance.**

When historian Diana Bishop opens an alchemical manuscript in the Bodleian Library, it's an unwelcome intrusion of magic into her carefully ordered life. Though Diana is a witch of impeccable lineage, the violent death of her parents while she was still a child convinced her that human fear is more potent than any witchcraft. Now Diana has unwittingly exposed herself to a world she's kept at bay for years; one of powerful witches, creative, destructive daemons and long-lived vampires. 

Sensing the significance of Diana's discovery, the creatures gather in Oxford, among them the enigmatic Matthew Clairmont, a vampire genticist. Diana is inexplicably drawn to Matthew and, in a shadowy world of half-truths and old enmities, ties herself to him without fully understanding the ancient line they are crossing.

As they begin to unlock the secrets of the manuscript and their feelings for each other deepen, so the fragile balance of peace unravels.

books.title: Forward the Foundation
books.author: Isaac Asimov
books.desc:
During the whole Foundation series, one man has always had his hand in the development of a galaxy. Merely hinted at in previous books, visited off and on for historical background - finally here delved into as deep as one can go - the demystified Hari Seldon. This follows about 40 years of his life, and traces his progress in the development of Psychohistory - the pseudo-mathematical science that would one day save the galaxy. 

If you have read the Foundation series, either in it's entirety or just pieces, this is a must read. It also (if memory serves) is the last book Asimov wrote before his death - the final pages describing Hari Seldon's final moments of life mirroring his own. A truly beautiful read.

books.title: The Windup Girl
books.author: Paolo Bacigalupi
books.desc: What Happens when bio-terrorism becomes a tool for corporate profits? And what happens when said bio-terrorism forces humanity to the cusp of post-human evolution? In The Windup Girl, award-winning author Paolo Bacigalupi returns to the world of "The Calorie Man"( Theodore Sturgeon Memorial Award-winner, Hugo Award nominee, 2006) and "Yellow Card Man" (Hugo Award nominee, 2007) in order to address these questions.

books.author: C. S. Lewis
books.desc: First broadcast as informal radio "talks" and later published as three separate books, The Case for Christianity, Christian Behaviour, and Beyond Personality are presented together in Mere Christianity. In his remarkably direct and accessible style, the renowned Christian apologist shows how the power of Christianity manifests itself -- not in any single denomination but as "mere" Christianity, a total force. For Lewis sets out to prove only that "in the center of each there is something, or a Someone, who against all divergencies of belief, all differences of temperament, all memories of mutual persecution, speaks with the same voice." - Back cover.

books.desc: Inside Out & Back Again is a verse novel by Thanhha Lai. The book was awarded the 2011 National Book Award for Young People's Literature and one of the two Newbery Honors. The novel was based on her first year in the United States, as a ten-year-old girl who spoke no English in 1975.

books.title: Cujo
books.author: Stephen King
books.desc: Cujo (/ˈkjuːdʒoʊ/) is a 1981 psychological horror novel by American writer Stephen King about a rabid Saint Bernard. The novel won the British Fantasy Award in 1982 and was made into a film in 1983.

books.title: The Long Walk
books.author: Stephen King
books.desc:
The Long Walk is a dystopian horror novel by American writer Stephen King, published in 1979, under the pseudonym Richard Bachman. It was collected in 1985 in the hardcover omnibus The Bachman Books, and has seen several reprints since, as both paperback and hardback.

Set in a future dystopian America, ruled by a totalitarian and militaristic dictator, the plot revolves around the contestants of a grueling, annual walking contest. In 2000, the American Library Association listed The Long Walk as one of the 100 best books for teenage readers published between 1966 and 2000.

---

Also contained in:

- [The Bachman Books](https://openlibrary.org/works/OL24796729W)

books.desc: Their Eyes Were Watching God (1937) is a classic Harlem Renaissance novel by American writer Zora Neale Hurston. The novel follows Janie Crawford as she recounts the story of her life as she journeys from a naive teenager to a woman in control of her destiny.

books.title: Men at Arms
books.author: Terry Pratchett
books.desc:
"Unadulterated fun." —San Francisco Chronicle

"Pratchett has now moved beyond the limits of humorous fantasy, and should be recognized as one of the more significant contemporary English-language satirists." —Publishers Weekly

The fifteenth novel in the Discworld series from acclaimed New York Times bestselling author Sir Terry Pratchett, featuring a lycanthropic recruit and a sword in a stone!

Corporal Carrot has been promoted! He’s now in charge of the new recruits guarding Ankh-Morpork, Discworld’s greatest city, from Barbarian Tribes, Miscellaneous Marauders, unlicensed Thieves, and such. It’s a big job, particularly for an adopted dwarf. But an even bigger job awaits. An ancient document has just revealed that Ankh-Morpork, ruled for decades by Disorganized crime, has a secret sovereign! And his name is Carrot . . .

And so begins the most awesome epic encounter of all time, or at least all afternoon, in which the fate of a city—indeed of the universe itself!—depends on a young man’s courage, an ancient sword’s magic, and a three-legged poodle’s bladder.

books.author: 戴维·迈尔斯
books.desc: 戴维·迈尔斯的《社会心理学》，教材级的实证心理学，理解社会与自我。

books.title: 影响力
books.author: 罗伯特·西奥迪尼
books.desc: 西奥迪尼总结互惠、承诺、社会认同等六大影响力原则，说服与防骗都适用。

books.title: 怪诞行为学
books.author: 丹·艾瑞里
books.desc: 行为经济学家揭示理性背后的非理性，认识决策中的陷阱。

books.title: 黑天鹅
books.author: 纳西姆·塔勒布
books.desc: 塔勒布讨论不可预测的重大“黑天鹅”事件及其冲击，风险思维启蒙。

books.title: 反脆弱
books.author: 纳西姆·塔勒布
books.desc: 在波动与不确定性中反而获益的“反脆弱”思想，塔勒布代表作。

books.title: 价值
books.author: 张磊
books.desc: 高瓴创始人张磊的长期主义投资哲学，理解价值投资的方法与心法。

books.title: 股票大作手回忆录
books.author: 埃德温·勒菲弗
books.desc: 以传奇交易员利弗莫尔为原型的投资回忆录，投机市场的经典之作。

books.title: 基金定投
books.author: 理财魔方
books.desc: 讲解基金定投的原理与实操，理财入门读物。

books.title: 哈利·波特与魔法石
books.author: J.K.罗琳
books.desc: 11岁男孩哈利得知自己是巫师，进入霍格沃茨魔法学校，奇幻经典首部。

books.title: 哈利·波特与密室
books.author: J.K.罗琳
books.desc: 《哈利·波特》第二部，密室之谜与蛇怪传说。

books.title: 哈利·波特与阿兹卡班的囚徒
books.author: J.K.罗琳
books.desc: 《哈利·波特》第三部，阿兹卡班囚徒小天狼星的出现。

books.title: 纳尼亚传奇
books.author: C.S.刘易斯
books.desc: 四个孩子穿过衣橱进入纳尼亚魔法世界，与狮子阿斯兰共同冒险，经典奇幻。

books.title: 魔戒
books.author: J.R.R.托尔金
books.desc: 弗罗多与护戒远征队踏上摧毁魔戒的旅程，现代奇幻文学的开山之作。

books.title: 长安十二时辰
books.author: 马伯庸
books.desc: 长安上元夜十二时辰内，死囚张小敬与少年李必联手追查一场惊天阴谋。

books.title: 沉默的巡游
books.author: 东野圭吾
books.desc: 多年未解的少女失踪案，在一场小镇巡游后迎来转机，东野圭吾温情推理。

books.title: 恶意
books.author: 东野圭吾
books.desc: 畅销书作家被杀，凶手很快认罪，然而动机层层反转，恶意令人不寒而栗。

books.title: 放学后
books.author: 东野圭吾
books.desc: 女高中生在校园更衣室被杀，密室中的谜团，东野圭吾出道代表作。

books.title: 新参者
books.author: 东野圭吾
books.desc: 东京人形町接连发生命案，刑警加贺恭一郎用温情推理还原真相，治愈系本格。

books.title: 岛上书店（新版）
books.author: 加布瑞埃拉·泽文
books.desc: 加布瑞埃拉·泽文《岛上书店》新版，一家书店治愈孤独的温暖故事。

books.title: 月亮与六便士（新版）
books.author: 毛姆
books.desc: 毛姆《月亮与六便士》新版，理想与现实的抉择，追逐艺术之梦。

books.title: 面纱
books.author: 毛姆
books.desc: 凯蒂在婚姻与背叛中历经幻灭，远赴疫区后完成自我救赎，毛姆的成长之作。

books.title: 刀锋
books.author: 毛姆
books.desc: 拉里放弃安逸生活，踏上漫长而深刻的精神求索之路，毛姆的代表作。

books.title: 悉达多
books.author: 赫尔曼·黑塞
books.desc: 婆罗门之子悉达多舍弃一切，历经苦行、尘世与河流，寻得觉悟，黑塞的诗意哲思。

books.title: 荒原狼
books.author: 赫尔曼·黑塞
books.desc: “荒原狼”体内同时住着人性与狼性，在分裂中挣扎求索，黑塞的现代主义经典。

books.title: 纳尔齐斯与歌尔德蒙
books.author: 赫尔曼·黑塞
books.desc: 理性沉稳的纳尔齐斯与感性放纵的歌尔德蒙，两条道路映照人生的两极，黑塞力作。

books.title: 情人
books.author: 玛格丽特·杜拉斯
books.desc: 少女与年长的中国情人在法属殖民地的禁忌之恋，杜拉斯关于欲望与记忆的告白。

books.title: 追忆似水年华
books.author: 马塞尔·普鲁斯特
books.desc: 以绵密意识流追忆童年、爱情与时光，普鲁斯特的皇皇巨著。

books.title: 丰乳肥臀
books.author: 莫言
books.desc: 母亲上官鲁氏含辛茹苦养育子女，在苦难中支撑家族，莫言笔下的女性与土地。

books.title: 檀香刑
books.author: 莫言
books.desc: 借“檀香刑”这一酷刑，写清末民间戏班与官府、反抗与牺牲，莫言的历史小说。

books.title: 生死疲劳
books.author: 莫言
books.desc: 地主西门闹经历六世轮回，见证半个世纪的乡村巨变，荒诞与深刻并存的魔幻之作。

books.title: 蛙
books.author: 莫言
books.desc: 乡村女医生万心大半生为接生奔忙，计划生育背景下的个体命运，莫言获诺奖前的重要作品。

books.title: 呐喊（纪念版）
books.author: 鲁迅
books.desc: 鲁迅《呐喊》纪念版，收录《狂人日记》等经典短篇。

books.title: 狂人日记
books.author: 鲁迅
books.desc: 借“狂人”之眼，看尽“吃人”的旧礼教，鲁迅第一篇白话小说，震聋发聩。

books.title: 彷徨（纪念版）
books.author: 鲁迅
books.desc: 鲁迅《彷徨》纪念版，收录《祝福》《伤逝》等作品。

books.title: 故事新编
books.author: 鲁迅
books.desc: 以神话和历史为素材的短篇小说集，收录《补天》《奔月》《铸剑》《理水》等八篇。古人血肉丰满，古今交融，充满反讽与幽默。

books.title: 野草
books.author: 鲁迅
books.desc: 鲁迅散文诗集，二十三篇短小精悍的哲思之作。'于浩歌狂热之际中寒，于天上看见深渊'，是鲁迅最孤独最深刻的文字。

books.title: 茶馆
books.author: 老舍
books.desc: 裕泰茶馆五十年兴衰，三幕话剧。一个茶馆看尽三个时代的变迁，'莫谈国事'四个字道尽乱世辛酸。

books.title: 湘行散记
books.author: 沈从文
books.desc: 沈从文回湘西途中写下的游记散文，十二个篇章。沅水流域的水手、妓女、兵士，构成一幅鲜活的湘西风情画。

books.title: 人·兽·鬼
books.author: 钱钟书
books.desc: 钱钟书短篇小说集，收录《上帝的梦》《猫》《灵感》《纪念》四篇。讽刺与机智并存，是钱钟书小说艺术的另一面向。

books.title: 写在人生边上
books.author: 钱钟书
books.desc: 钱钟书第一本散文集，十篇哲理散文。'人生据说是一部大书'，钱钟书以博喻和反讽写透人情世态。

books.title: 金锁记
books.author: 张爱玲
books.desc: 曹七巧被黄金枷锁压垮一生的故事。张爱玲笔下最惨烈的女性悲剧，'三十年来她戴着黄金的枷，她用那沉重的枷角劈杀了几个人'。

books.title: 倾城之恋
books.author: 张爱玲
books.desc: 白流苏与范柳原在香港沦陷中的爱情。一座城市的倾覆成就了一对凡人的姻缘，张爱玲最雅俗共赏的中篇。

books.title: 半生缘
books.author: 张爱玲
books.desc: 沈世钧与顾曼桢被时代和命运拆散的爱情。'我们回不去了'，张爱玲最令人心碎的长篇。

books.title: 红玫瑰与白玫瑰
books.author: 张爱玲
books.desc: 振保生命中的两个女人——红玫瑰热烈奔放，白玫瑰温婉无趣。'娶了红玫瑰，久而久之红的变了墙上的一抹蚊子血'。

books.title: 小团圆
books.author: 张爱玲
books.desc: 张爱玲半自传体长篇小说，遗作出版。九莉与燕山、邵之雍的情感纠葛，是张爱玲对自己一生的清算。

books.title: 色，戒
books.author: 张爱玲
books.desc: 王佳芝刺杀易先生的故事，被李安改编成电影。'到女人心里的路通过阴道'，张爱玲最冷的短篇。

books.title: 呼兰河传
books.author: 萧红
books.desc: 萧红自传体长篇小说，回忆东北小城呼兰河的生活。我与祖父的后花园、大泥坑、小团圆媳妇的悲剧，是萧红最后的杰作。

books.title: 生死场
books.author: 萧红
books.desc: 东北农民在日寇侵略下的苦难与抗争。'死人走在活人中，活人准备着死'，萧红以女性笔触写透生之坚韧与死之漠然。

books.title: 城南旧事
books.author: 林海音
books.desc: 小英子在北京城南的童年回忆：秀贞、妞儿、偷儿、兰姨娘、宋妈。林海音以孩童视角写尽旧北京的人情冷暖。

books.title: 家
books.author: 巴金
books.desc: 高家三兄弟在封建大家庭中的命运挣扎。觉新的懦弱、觉民的反抗、觉慧的出走，是五四青年的精神缩影。

books.title: 春
books.author: 巴金
books.desc: 《家》的续篇，蕙、淑英等年轻女性在封建礼教下的悲剧与反抗。'春天是我们的'，巴金写出了青春的力量。

books.title: 秋
books.author: 巴金
books.desc: 《激流三部曲》终篇，高家彻底衰落。'没有一个完备的团圆'，巴金写尽封建大家庭的必然崩溃。

books.title: 寒夜
books.author: 巴金
books.desc: 抗战后期重庆，小公务员汪文宣在婆媳矛盾和贫病交加中死去。巴金最现实主义的杰作，写尽小人物的辛酸。

books.title: 子夜
books.author: 茅盾
books.desc: 民族资本家吴荪甫在十里洋场的兴衰。茅盾以社会科学家的笔触，全景式展现1930年代中国都市的经济与阶级。

books.title: 林家铺子
books.author: 茅盾
books.desc: 小商人林老板在帝国主义和官僚资本压迫下破产的故事。茅盾最精炼的中篇，写尽30年代民族商业的困境。

books.title: 雷雨
books.author: 曹禺
books.desc: 周鲁两家三十年间的恩怨情仇，一天之内爆发。曹禺的处女作，中国现代话剧成熟的标志。

books.title: 日出
books.author: 曹禺
books.desc: 陈白露在交际花生活中的挣扎与毁灭。'太阳出来了，黑暗留在后面，但是太阳不是我们的'，曹禺写尽都市腐烂。

books.title: 原野
books.author: 曹禺
books.desc: 仇虎从逃狱到复仇的悲剧。曹禺最原始野性的剧作，融合表现主义与民间气息。

books.title: 北京人
books.author: 曹禺
books.desc: 曾家三代在衰败中挣扎。曹禺最后一部杰作，'要走，要走到远远的地方去'。

books.title: 梦里花落知多少
books.author: 三毛
books.desc: 荷西去世后三毛的悲痛与思念。'花落花飞飞满天，红消香断有谁怜'，是三毛最心碎的作品。

books.title: 送你一匹马
books.author: 三毛
books.desc: 三毛与读者的书信和散文。'书中Margarita有一个好父亲'，温柔真挚。

books.title: 万水千山走遍
books.author: 三毛
books.desc: 三毛中南美洲旅行记。墨西哥、危地马拉、厄瓜多尔、秘鲁，三毛眼中的拉丁美洲。

books.title: 我的宝贝
books.author: 三毛
books.desc: 三毛收藏的各种小物件的故事。铜钱、旧衣架、小石像，每件宝贝都有一段回忆。

books.title: 滚滚红尘
books.author: 三毛
books.desc: 三毛唯一的电影剧本，邵华与能才在乱世中的爱情。被严浩改编成电影，林青霞张曼玉主演。

books.title: 在细雨中呼喊
books.author: 余华
books.desc: 孙光林的童年与少年回忆。余华第一部长篇，'我不再装模作样地拥有很多朋友，而是回到了孤单之中'。

books.title: 现实一种
books.author: 余华
books.desc: 山岗山峰兄弟两家的暴力循环。余华早期最冷酷的中篇，血腥而精准。

books.title: 红高粱家族
books.author: 莫言
books.desc: 高密东北乡，我爷爷我奶奶的抗日传奇。莫言以天马行空的叙事和感官描写，开启了中国文学的新境界。

books.title: 酒国
books.author: 莫言
books.desc: 调查员丁钩儿到酒国市调查吃婴案。莫言最荒诞的讽刺小说。

books.title: 长恨歌
books.author: 王安忆
books.desc: 上海小姐王琦瑶四十年的情与爱。王安忆获茅盾文学奖，'一个女人四十年的情与爱'。

books.title: 繁花
books.author: 金宇澄
books.desc: 上海弄堂里阿宝、沪生、小毛等人的故事。金宇澄获茅盾文学奖，用沪语写就的上海城市史诗。

books.title: 额尔古纳河右岸
books.author: 迟子建
books.desc: 鄂温克族最后一位酋长女人的自述。迟子建获茅盾文学奖，写尽游牧民族的衰落与坚守。

books.title: 世界上所有的夜晚
books.author: 迟子建
books.desc: 丈夫意外去世后，'我'到小镇疗愈，却遇到更多苦难。迟子建最私人也最普世的中篇。

books.title: 秦腔
books.author: 贾平凹
books.desc: 清风街夏天礼、夏天义、夏天智三兄弟的故事。贾平凹获茅盾文学奖，写尽乡村的衰败。

books.title: 废都
books.author: 贾平凹
books.desc: 西京城里庄之蝶等四大名人的情与欲。曾被列为禁书，是贾平凹最具争议的作品。

books.title: 受活
books.author: 阎连科
books.desc: 受庄里残障村民被县领导组织成'绝术团'巡回演出赚钱。阎连科的'黑色祈祷'。

books.title: 我与父辈
books.author: 阎连科
books.desc: 阎连科回忆父亲、伯父、叔父三位父辈。'我从未这样悲伤过'，是阎连科最朴素最动人的作品。

books.title: 日光流年
books.author: 阎连科
books.desc: 三姓村人在四十岁寿命的诅咒下与命运抗争。阎连科的'神话'。

books.title: 一句顶一万句
books.author: 刘震云
books.desc: 杨百成、牛爱国两代人寻找'说得着的人'的故事。刘震云获茅盾文学奖，'一个人的孤独不是孤独，一个人找另一个人的孤独才是孤独'。

books.title: 一地鸡毛
books.author: 刘震云
books.desc: 小林家的白菜、豆腐、单位分房。刘震云写尽小市民的日常琐碎，'一地鸡毛'成了生活的代名词。

books.title: 我不是潘金莲
books.author: 刘震云
books.desc: 李雪莲为纠正一句话告状二十年。刘震云最讽刺的中篇，被冯小刚改编成电影。

books.title: 温故一九四二
books.author: 刘震云
books.desc: 1942年河南大饥荒，三百万人饿死。刘震云的调查体小说，'我想知道我从哪里来'。

books.title: 一日三秋
books.author: 刘震云
books.desc: 梨花和延津人的故事，融合魔幻与现实。刘震云最新长篇，'一日三秋，度日如年'。

books.title: 推拿
books.author: 毕飞宇
books.desc: 沙宗琪推拿中心盲人们的生活与爱情。毕飞宇获茅盾文学奖，'他们的世界也有光'。

books.title: 青衣
books.author: 毕飞宇
books.desc: 筱燕秋与嫦娥角色纠缠一生的故事。毕飞宇写透戏曲演员的痴迷与悲剧。

books.title: 妻妾成群
books.author: 苏童
books.desc: 女学生颂莲嫁入陈府做四姨太，在妻妾争宠中走向疯狂。苏童最著名的中篇，被张艺谋改编为《大红灯笼高高挂》。

books.title: 黄雀记
books.author: 苏童
books.desc: 保润、柳生、仙女三个年轻人二十年间的恩怨。苏童获茅盾文学奖，'黄雀在后'。

books.title: 河岸
books.author: 苏童
books.desc: 少年童下河在枫杨树乡的成长。苏童最自传性的长篇。

books.title: 三体Ⅱ：黑暗森林
books.author: 刘慈欣
books.desc: 宇宙就是一座黑暗森林，每个文明都是带枪的猎人。罗辑建立黑暗森林威慑，与三体文明对峙。刘慈欣的巅峰。

books.title: 三体Ⅲ：死神永生
books.author: 刘慈欣
books.desc: 云天明的三个童话、二维化太阳系、程心与关一帆在小宇宙的结局。三部曲终章，'给岁月以文明，而不是给文明以岁月'。

books.title: 超新星纪元
books.author: 刘慈欣
books.desc: 超新星爆发后所有成年人死去，世界交给孩子。刘慈欣最有想象力的长篇。

books.title: 乡村教师
books.author: 刘慈欣
books.desc: 黄土高原上的乡村教师临终前教给学生的牛顿三大定律，拯救了地球文明。最朴素也最震撼的科幻。

books.title: 朝闻道
books.author: 刘慈欣
books.desc: 科学家们用生命换取宇宙真理。'朝闻道，夕死可矣'，是刘慈欣最动人的短篇。

books.title: 北京折叠
books.author: 郝景芳
books.desc: 北京被分成三个空间，折叠轮换生活。郝景芳获雨果奖中短篇小说奖。

books.title: 两京十五日
books.author: 马伯庸
books.desc: 朱瞻基十五天从南京赶回北京继位。马伯庸最紧凑的历史小说。

books.title: 风起陇西
books.author: 马伯庸
books.desc: 三国时期蜀汉与曹魏的谍战。马伯庸处女作，'间谍就在你身边'。

books.title: 明朝那些事儿
books.author: 当年明月
books.desc: 从1344年朱元璋出生到1644年崇祯自缢，三百年明朝史。当年明月以小说笔法写历史，是最畅销的历史普及读物。

books.title: 国史大纲
books.author: 钱穆
books.desc: 钱穆在抗战流亡中写就的中国通史。'所谓对其本国已往历史略有所知者，尤必附随一种对其本国已往历史之温情与敬意'。

books.title: 近代中国社会的新陈代谢
books.author: 陈旭麓
books.desc: 从鸦片战争到五四运动，中国社会结构的深层变迁。陈旭麓的遗作，近代史研究的典范。

books.title: 天朝的崩溃
books.author: 茅海建
books.publisher: 生活·读书·新知三联书店
books.desc: 鸦片战争再研究，从琦善、林则徐的视角重审战争。茅海建最具颠覆性的近代史著作。

books.title: 万古江河
books.author: 许倬云
books.desc: 从新石器时代到今天，中国文化的发展历程。许倬云以全球视野写中国史。

books.title: 干校六记
books.author: 杨绛
books.publisher: 生活·读书·新知三联书店
books.desc: 杨绛在文革干校的劳动生活。'我双手撑着地，慢慢站起来'，克制冷静中见深情。

books.title: 洗澡
books.author: 杨绛
books.desc: 解放后知识分子思想改造的故事。杨绛最讽刺也最宽容的长篇。

books.title: 傅雷家书
books.author: 傅雷
books.publisher: 生活·读书·新知三联书店
books.desc: 傅雷夫妇给儿子傅聪、傅敏的家信。艺术、做人、家国，是中国父母最真挚的教子书。

books.title: 我与地坛
books.author: 史铁生
books.desc: 史铁生双腿瘫痪后在地坛公园的思考。'死是一件不必急于求成的事，死是一个必然会降临的节日'。

books.title: 病隙碎笔
books.author: 史铁生
books.desc: 史铁生在病痛间隙写下的哲思随笔。关于残疾、爱情、信仰、命运，是中国当代最深刻的散文。

books.title: 务虚笔记
books.author: 史铁生
books.desc: 史铁生第一部长篇，写作与生命的寓言。'我是一个行者，我的路在脚下'。

books.title: 命若琴弦
books.author: 史铁生
books.desc: 盲师徒弹三弦为生，师父说弹断一千根琴弦就能看见光明。史铁生最动人的中篇。

books.title: 爱你就像爱生命
books.author: 王小波
books.desc: 王小波给李银河的情书。'你好哇，李银河'，最浪漫也最真诚的情书。

books.title: 谈美
books.author: 朱光潜
books.desc: 朱光潜给青年的第十三封信。'美是主观的，也是客观的'，中国最好的美学入门书。

books.title: 人间词话
books.author: 王国维
books.desc: 王国维的词学批评。境界说：'古今之成大事业大学问者，必经过三种之境界'。

books.title: 美的历程
books.author: 李泽厚
books.desc: 从远古图腾到明清工艺，中国美学的发展历程。李泽厚最有影响力的美学著作。

books.title: 高效能人士的七个习惯
books.author: 史蒂芬·柯维
books.desc: 积极主动、以终为始、要事第一、双赢思维、知彼解己、统合综效、不断更新。最经典的自我管理。

books.title: 人性的弱点
books.author: 戴尔·卡耐基
books.desc: 如何赢得朋友、影响他人、改变他人。卡耐基的经典，畅销全球近百年。

books.title: 从0到1
books.author: 彼得·蒂尔
books.desc: PayPal创始人彼得·蒂尔的创业哲学。'竞争是留给失败者的'，硅谷创投圣经。

books.title: 激荡三十年
books.author: 吴晓波
books.desc: 1978-2008中国企业的风雨三十年。吴晓波写尽中国企业家的沉浮。

books.title: 梦的解析
books.author: 弗洛伊德
books.desc: 弗洛伊德精神分析学奠基之作。梦是愿望的满足，潜意识理论的起点。

books.title: 爱的艺术
books.author: 弗洛姆
books.desc: 爱是一门艺术，一种能力。'不成熟的爱是因为我需要你所以我爱你，成熟的爱是因为我爱你所以我需要你'。

books.title: 逃避自由
books.author: 弗洛姆
books.desc: 现代人在自由面前的焦虑与逃避。弗洛姆从心理学分析法西斯主义的社会心理根源。

books.title: 幸福之路
books.author: 罗素
books.desc: 罗素写给普通人的幸福指南。避免欲望的过度膨胀，在工作和热情中找到幸福。

books.title: 西方哲学史
books.author: 罗素
books.desc: 从古希腊到现代，西方哲学的发展历程。罗素诺贝尔文学奖获奖作品，文笔优美。

books.title: 鼠疫
books.author: 加缪
books.desc: 奥兰城突发鼠疫，里厄医生和人们在封城中的抗争。在荒诞中选择责任与爱。

books.title: 西西弗神话
books.author: 加缪
books.desc: 推石上山的西西弗是荒诞英雄。'应当想象西西弗是幸福的'。加缪的哲学随笔。

books.title: 存在与虚无
books.author: 萨特
books.publisher: 生活·读书·新知三联书店
books.desc: 萨特存在主义哲学巨著。'存在先于本质'，人被判定为自由。

books.title: 查拉图斯特拉如是说
books.author: 尼采
books.publisher: 生活·读书·新知三联书店
books.desc: 查拉图斯特拉下山向世人传授超人哲学。'上帝死了'，尼采最有文学性的哲学著作。

books.author: 乔治·奥威尔
books.desc: 大洋国温斯顿在老大哥统治下的思想罪。'战争即和平，自由即奴役，无知即力量'。反乌托邦三部曲之首。

books.title: 动物农场
books.author: 乔治·奥威尔
books.desc: 曼纳农场的动物造反推翻人类，却被猪篡夺。'所有动物一律平等，但有些动物比其他动物更加平等'。

books.title: 美丽新世界
books.author: 赫胥黎
books.desc: 福特纪元六三二年的世界，人们被基因和药物驯化。奥威尔警告我们憎恨什么，赫胥黎警告我们爱上什么。

books.title: 群山回唱
books.author: 卡勒德·胡赛尼
books.desc: 兄妹阿卜杜拉和帕丽被分离的故事，跨越六十年三个国家。

books.title: 永别了，武器
books.author: 海明威
books.desc: 亨利中尉与凯瑟琳在一战中的爱情与逃亡。'世界打碎了每一个人，然后许多人在破碎处变得坚强'。

books.title: 丧钟为谁而鸣
books.author: 海明威
books.desc: 罗伯特·乔丹在西班牙内战中炸桥的三天。'没有人是一座孤岛……丧钟为谁而鸣，它为你而鸣'。

books.title: 悲惨世界
books.author: 雨果
books.desc: 冉阿让因偷面包坐十九年牢，后在主教感化下成为善人。雨果最宏大的人道主义杰作。

books.title: 巴黎圣母院
books.author: 雨果
books.desc: 敲钟人卡西莫多与吉普赛女郎爱斯梅拉达在巴黎圣母院的悲剧。雨果的浪漫主义经典。

books.title: 基督山伯爵
books.author: 大仲马
books.desc: 爱德蒙·唐泰斯被陷害入狱十四年后复仇。'等待和希望'，大仲马最畅销的冒险小说。

books.title: 三个火枪手
books.author: 大仲马
books.desc: 达达尼昂与阿托斯、波尔多斯、阿拉密斯的冒险。'人人为我，我为人人'。

books.title: 茶花女
books.author: 小仲马
books.desc: 玛格丽特与阿尔芒的爱情悲剧。小仲马根据自己与玛丽·杜普莱西的经历写成。

books.title: 复活
books.author: 列夫·托尔斯泰
books.desc: 聂赫留朵夫在法庭上见到被自己始乱终弃的玛丝洛娃，开始灵魂救赎。托尔斯泰最后的长篇。

books.title: 卡拉马佐夫兄弟
books.author: 陀思妥耶夫斯基
books.desc: 老卡拉马佐夫被杀，四个儿子各怀鬼胎。陀思妥耶夫斯基最后的杰作，宗教大法官的篇章震撼人心。

books.title: 白痴
books.author: 陀思妥耶夫斯基
books.desc: 梅诗金公爵纯洁如白痴，却在彼得堡的世俗中被摧毁。

books.title: 变形记
books.author: 卡夫卡
books.desc: 格里高尔一天早上变成了大甲虫。'一天早晨，格里高尔·萨姆沙从不安的睡梦中醒来，发现自己躺在床上变成了一只巨大的甲虫'。

books.title: 审判
books.author: 卡夫卡
books.desc: 约瑟夫·K在三十岁生日那天被捕，却不知道自己犯了什么罪。

books.title: 城堡
books.author: 卡夫卡
books.desc: K大雪中来到城堡下的村庄，永远无法进入城堡。

books.title: 尤利西斯
books.author: 乔伊斯
books.desc: 布卢姆在都柏林一天的漫游，对应荷马史诗奥德赛。意识流文学的巅峰。

books.title: 不能承受的生命之轻
books.author: 米兰·昆德拉
books.desc: 托马斯、特蕾莎、萨宾娜在布拉格之春前后的爱与命运。'永恒轮回是一种神秘的想法……最沉重的负担同时也成了最强盛的生命力的影像'。

books.title: 玩笑
books.author: 米兰·昆德拉
books.desc: 路德维克因为一张玩笑的明信片毁了一生。昆德拉第一部小说。

books.title: 没有人给他写信的上校
books.author: 加西亚·马尔克斯
books.desc: 上校每天等退休金等了五十六年。'吃什么？''吃屎'。马尔克斯最苦涩的中篇。

books.title: 雪国
books.author: 川端康成
books.desc: 岛村三赴雪国与驹子、叶子的情缘。'穿过县界长长的隧道，便是雪国'。川端康成诺贝尔文学奖代表作。

books.title: 千只鹤
books.author: 川端康成
books.desc: 菊治与太田夫人、文子的情感纠葛。川端康成最美的中篇。

books.title: 古都
books.author: 川端康成
books.desc: 千重子在京都的成长，双胞胎苗子的出现。川端康成最后的诺贝尔文学奖作品。

books.title: 海边的卡夫卡
books.author: 村上春树
books.desc: 田村卡夫卡十五岁离家出走，中田老人奇妙的旅程。村上春树最奇幻的长篇。

books.title: 1Q84
books.author: 村上春树
books.desc: 青豆和天吾在1984年的平行世界里相遇。村上春树最 ambitious 的长篇。

books.title: 刺杀骑士团长
books.author: 村上春树
books.desc: 免色先生、雨田具彦的画、白色斯巴鲁。村上春树最新长篇。

books.title: 且听风吟
books.author: 村上春树
books.desc: 村上春树处女作，'我'在夏天的回忆。'不存在十全十美的文章，如同不存在彻头彻尾的绝望'。

books.title: 舞！舞！舞！
books.author: 村上春树
books.desc: 五反田雪、羊男、宾馆。村上春树最迷幻的长篇。

books.title: 秘密
books.author: 东野圭吾
books.desc: 妻子直子在车祸中灵魂进入女儿藻奈美的身体。东野圭吾最催泪的设定。

books.title: 麒麟之翼
books.author: 东野圭吾
books.desc: 加贺恭一郎在麒麟雕像下调查杀人案。

books.title: 祈祷落幕时
books.author: 东野圭吾
books.desc: 加贺恭一郎的母亲失踪案与杀人案。

books.title: 流星之绊
books.author: 东野圭吾
books.desc: 三兄妹父母被杀，十四年追查凶手。

books.title: 信
books.author: 东野圭吾
books.desc: 杀人犯的弟弟在社会歧视中挣扎。东野圭吾最社会派的小说。

books.title: 时生
books.author: 东野圭吾
books.desc: 时生穿越回二十年前和父亲一起。'时生，我在花屋敷等你'。

books.title: 聊斋志异
books.author: 蒲松龄
books.desc: 蒲松龄写鬼写妖高人一等，刺贪刺虐入木三分。聂小倩、画皮、婴宁。

books.title: 儒林外史
books.author: 吴敬梓
books.desc: 范进中举、严监生临死灯盏点两茎灯草。吴敬梓讽刺科举制度的长篇。

books.title: 封神演义
books.author: 许仲琳
books.desc: 武王伐纣，姜子牙封神。哪吒、杨戬、妲己。

books.title: 镜花缘
books.author: 李汝珍
books.desc: 唐敖游历海外各国。李汝珍最有想象力的古典小说。

books.title: 论语
books.author: 孔子弟子
books.desc: 孔子及其弟子言行录。'学而时习之，不亦说乎''己所不欲，勿施于人'。

books.title: 道德经
books.author: 老子
books.desc: 老子五千言。'道可道，非常道''上善若水，水善利万物而不争'。

books.title: 庄子
books.author: 庄周
books.desc: 庄周梦蝶、逍遥游、齐物论。'吾生也有涯，而知也无涯'。

books.title: 孙子兵法
books.author: 孙武
books.desc: 孙武十三篇兵书。'知己知彼，百战不殆''兵者，诡道也'。

books.title: 曾国藩家书
books.author: 曾国藩
books.desc: 曾国藩给家人的书信。修身、齐家、治国，'结硬寨，打呆仗'。

books.title: 一个人的朝圣
books.author: 蕾秋·乔伊斯
books.desc: 哈罗德徒步六百二十七英里去看狱中老友奎妮。一封来信、一个信念，他走过了英格兰，也走回了自己的内心。

books.title: 素食者
books.author: 韩江
books.desc: 英慧突然开始拒绝吃肉，家人从困惑到暴力，她一步步退向植物般的沉默。韩江布克国际文学奖获奖作。

books.title: 诗经
books.author: 佚名
books.desc: 中国最早的诗歌总集，三百零五篇。关关雎鸠、蒹葭苍苍、青青子衿，两千五百年前的风、雅、颂。

books.title: 菜根谭
books.author: 洪应明
books.desc: 明代洪应明著语录体散文集。'宠辱不惊，闲看庭前花开花落；去留无意，漫随天外云卷云舒'。

books.title: 瓦尔登湖
books.author: 亨利·戴维·梭罗
books.desc: 梭罗在瓦尔登湖畔独居两年的记录。'我步入丛林，因为我希望活得有意义'。超验主义经典。

books.title: 克林索尔的最后夏天
books.author: 赫尔曼·黑塞
books.desc: 黑塞在一战后的混乱中写成的自传式随笔。绘画、醉酒、青春、死亡，语言如迷幻诗。

books.title: 德米安
books.author: 赫尔曼·黑塞
books.desc: 少年辛克莱在德米安引导下寻找自我。'鸟要挣脱出壳。蛋就是世界。人要诞于世上，就得摧毁整个世界'。

books.title: 在轮下
books.author: 赫尔曼·黑塞
books.desc: 汉斯考入神学院却在教育机器压迫下崩溃。黑塞对应试教育的控诉。

books.title: 月亮和六便士
books.author: 威廉·毛姆
books.desc: 银行家思特里克兰德突然弃家出走，去塔希提画画至死。'满地都是六便士，他却抬头看见了月亮'。

books.title: 人性的枷锁
books.author: 威廉·毛姆
books.desc: 菲利普从童年到中年的成长，跛足、爱情、欲望、枷锁。毛姆半自传体长篇。

books.title: 理智与情感
books.author: 简·奥斯汀
books.desc: 达什伍德家两姐妹，埃莉诺理智、玛丽安热情。奥斯汀第一部出版的小说。

books.title: 爱玛
books.author: 简·奥斯汀
books.desc: 爱玛爱做媒，最后发现自己的归宿。奥斯汀最成熟的喜剧。

books.title: 劝导
books.author: 简·奥斯汀
books.desc: 安妮年轻时听从劝导拒绝了温特沃思，八年后他衣锦归来。奥斯汀最后一部小说。

books.title: 简·爱
books.author: 夏洛蒂·勃朗特
books.desc: 孤女简·爱与罗切斯特的爱情。'你以为我贫穷、低微、不美、矮小，我就没有灵魂没有心吗？'

books.title: 双城记
books.author: 查尔斯·狄更斯
books.desc: 伦敦与巴黎，梅尼特医生、代尔纳、卡尔顿在大革命中的命运。'这是最好的时代，这是最坏的时代'。

books.title: 远大前程
books.author: 查尔斯·狄更斯
books.desc: 匹普从铁匠学徒到伦敦绅士的成长与幻灭。狄更斯晚期最成熟的作品。

books.title: 雾都孤儿
books.author: 查尔斯·狄更斯
books.desc: 奥利弗在济贫院、贼窝中的挣扎。狄更斯第一部社会批判小说。

books.title: 大卫·科波菲尔
books.author: 查尔斯·狄更斯
books.desc: 大卫从孤儿到作家的成长。狄更斯自称'最宠爱的孩子'，半自传体。

books.title: 德伯家的苔丝
books.author: 托马斯·哈代
books.desc: 苔丝被亚雷玷污、被克莱抛弃，最后走向毁灭。'一个纯洁的女人'。

books.title: 无名的裘德
books.author: 托马斯·哈代
books.desc: 裘德想上大学却被阶级门槛挡在外面，与淑的爱情也不被容。哈代最悲剧的长篇。

books.title: 达洛维夫人
books.author: 弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫
books.desc: 克拉丽莎·达洛维一天的伦敦街头。'她自己就是那个时刻，那个顶点'。意识流经典。

books.title: 到灯塔去
books.author: 弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫
books.desc: 拉姆齐一家在苏格兰岛十年间的变化。窗、时光流逝、灯塔，三部曲结构。

books.title: 一间自己的房间
books.author: 弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫
books.desc: '女人要想写小说，必须有钱，再加一间自己的房间'。女性主义经典。

books.title: 金阁寺
books.author: 三岛由纪夫
books.desc: 沟口因金阁的美而纵火焚毁它。三岛根据真实事件写成，美与毁灭的极致。

books.title: 潮骚
books.author: 三岛由纪夫
books.desc: 渔村青年新治与宫田初江的纯洁爱情。三岛最阳光的小说。

books.title: 假面的告白
books.author: 三岛由纪夫
books.desc: 三岛半自传体，写一个青年对死亡、肉体、美的迷恋。成名作。

books.title: 斜阳
books.author: 太宰治
books.desc: 津田蔷薇一家在战后的没落。'斜阳族'一词由此而来。

books.title: 我是猫
books.author: 夏目漱石
books.desc: 以猫的视角观察苦沙弥先生和他的知识分子朋友。夏目漱石成名作，讽刺幽默。

books.title: 心
books.author: 夏目漱石
books.desc: 先生在朋友死后留下遗书，揭示自己的原罪。'人世间再没有像寂寞这样可怕的病了'。

books.title: 伊豆的舞女
books.author: 川端康成
books.desc: '我'在伊豆路上遇到巡回艺人，与舞女薰子的朦胧情愫。川端康成成名作。

books.title: 罗生门
books.author: 芥川龙之介
books.desc: 收录《罗生门》《竹林中》《鼻子》《杜子春》等。黑泽明《罗生门》原作。

books.title: 源氏物语
books.author: 紫式部
books.desc: 光源氏一生的情爱与命运。日本平安时代紫式部写就，世界最早的长篇小说。

books.title: 枕草子
books.author: 清少纳言
books.desc: 清少纳言在宫中的随笔。'春，黎明的时候最有意思'。与《源氏物语》并称平安文学双璧。

books.title: 银河铁道之夜
books.author: 宫泽贤治
books.desc: 乔万尼在银河中与康帕内拉坐火车旅行。宫泽贤治最美的童话，'真正的幸福是什么'。

books.title: 厨房
books.author: 吉本芭娜娜
books.desc: 樱井在厨房中治愈丧亲之痛。吉本芭娜娜成名作，日本当代治愈系小说。

books.title: 失乐园
books.author: 渡边淳一
books.desc: 久木与凛子在不伦之恋中走向殉情。渡边淳一最轰动的小说。

books.title: 沉默
books.author: 远藤周作
books.desc: 葡萄牙神父罗德里格斯在日本幕府迫害下的信仰挣扎。远藤周作代表作，'沉默的上帝'。

books.title: 小径分岔的花园
books.author: 豪尔赫·路易斯·博尔赫斯
books.desc: 间谍余准在花园中传递情报，时间像迷宫一样分岔。博尔赫斯最著名的短篇。

books.title: 阿莱夫
books.author: 豪尔赫·路易斯·博尔赫斯
books.desc: 阿莱夫是空间中包含一切点的点。博尔赫斯短篇小说集。

books.title: 看不见的城市
books.author: 伊塔洛·卡尔维诺
books.desc: 马可·波罗向忽必烈汗描述五十五座城市。'城市就像一块海绵，吸汲着这些不断涌流的记忆的潮水'。

books.title: 如果在冬夜，一个旅人
books.author: 伊塔洛·卡尔维诺
books.desc: 十个小说开头，一个读者在追寻完整的书。卡尔维诺最元小说的作品。

books.title: 玫瑰的名字
books.author: 安伯托·艾柯
books.desc: 中世纪修道院里连环谋杀。艾柯的博学侦探小说，符号学与神学的迷宫。

books.title: 在路上
books.author: 杰克·凯鲁亚克
books.desc: 萨尔与迪安横穿美国的公路旅行。'真正的人都是疯疯癫癫的，他们热爱生活'。垮掉的一代圣经。

books.title: 达摩流浪者
books.author: 杰克·凯鲁亚克
books.desc: 雷在加州山林中寻访禅道。'永远年轻，永远热泪盈眶'。

books.title: 宠儿
books.author: 托妮·莫里森
books.desc: 赛丝在俄亥俄州自由州被亡女'宠儿'鬼魂纠缠。莫里森诺贝尔文学奖代表作。

books.title: 使女的故事
books.author: 玛格丽特·阿特伍德
books.desc: 基列国中，奥芙弗雷德作为使女被征用生育。反乌托邦经典，被改编为热门剧集。

books.title: 逃离
books.author: 艾丽丝·门罗
books.desc: 八个女人逃离又回归的故事。门罗布克国际奖、诺贝尔文学奖代表作。

books.title: 心是孤独的猎手
books.author: 卡森·麦卡勒斯
books.desc: 小镇上，哑巴辛格被各怀心事的人当作倾诉对象。'心是孤独的猎手'。

books.title: 伤心咖啡馆之歌
books.author: 卡森·麦卡勒斯
books.desc: 爱密利亚小姐与李蒙表哥、马文·马西的三角怪恋。麦卡勒斯最著名的中篇。

books.title: 蒂凡尼的早餐
books.author: 杜鲁门·卡波蒂
books.desc: 霍莉·戈莱特利在纽约上流社会游走。'蒂凡尼是个让我不再害怕的地方'。

books.title: 冷血
books.author: 杜鲁门·卡波蒂
books.desc: 堪萨斯州农场四口被杀案，卡波蒂六年追踪凶手。'非虚构小说'开山之作。

books.title: 蝇王
books.author: 威廉·戈尔丁
books.desc: 一群男孩流落荒岛，从文明走向野蛮。戈尔丁诺贝尔文学奖代表作。

books.title: 巴黎伦敦落魄记
books.author: 乔治·奥威尔
books.desc: 奥威尔在巴黎做洗碗工、在伦敦流浪的经历。'贫穷的本质是磨灭未来'。

books.title: 向加泰罗尼亚致敬
books.author: 乔治·奥威尔
books.desc: 奥威尔参加西班牙内战的经历。'我那时才知道，左派报纸的谎言比右派还离谱'。

books.title: 给青年诗人的信
books.author: 莱内·马利亚·里尔克
books.desc: 里尔克给青年卡卜斯的十封信。'要对你心里所有还未解决的事有耐心'。

books.title: 恶心
books.author: 让-保罗·萨特
books.desc: 洛根丁在公园中突然感受到存在的荒谬。萨特存在主义小说代表作。

books.title: 生活在别处
books.author: 米兰·昆德拉
books.desc: 诗人雅罗米尔在青春与革命中的狂热与死亡。昆德拉获梅迪西奖。

books.title: 不朽
books.author: 米兰·昆德拉
books.desc: 阿涅丝、保罗、勃朗-生的三段爱情与不朽。昆德拉最哲学的小说。

books.title: 哈扎尔辞典
books.author: 米洛拉德·帕维奇
books.desc: 一部关于哈扎尔人改宗之谜的辞典小说，阴本阳本。'这是一部十万个读者会读出十万种读法的书'。

books.title: 佩德罗·巴拉莫
books.author: 胡安·鲁尔福
books.desc: 胡安赴科马拉寻父，发现全村都是幽灵。魔幻现实主义先驱，影响了马尔克斯。

books.title: 纸牌的秘密
books.author: 乔斯坦·贾德
books.desc: 汉密士在欧洲旅途中遇到一本神秘的圆顶纸牌故事。贾德继《苏菲的世界》后又一哲思童话。

books.title: 乔布斯传
books.author: 沃尔特·艾萨克森
books.desc: 乔布斯授权官方传记。从里德学院到苹果、皮克斯、回归，一个完美主义者的一生。

books.title: 崩溃
books.author: 贾雷德·戴蒙德
books.desc: 社会为何崩溃？复活节岛、玛雅、格陵兰。戴蒙德续作。

books.title: 昨日的世界
books.author: 斯蒂芬·茨威格
books.desc: 茨威格回忆战前欧洲的黄金时代。'我从来没有比在昨天更热爱欧洲，也从来没有比现在更对它绝望'。

books.title: 一个陌生女人的来信
books.author: 斯蒂芬·茨威格
books.desc: 一个女人用一生爱一个男人，临终写来一封信。茨威格最著名的中篇。

books.title: 人类群星闪耀时
books.author: 斯蒂芬·茨威格
books.publisher: 生活·读书·新知三联书店
books.desc: 十四个改变人类命运的瞬间：滑铁卢、南极探险、列宁封闭列车。茨威格最畅销的历史特写。
